intro_en: You will learn how to greet an elder politely with та and a friend casually with чи. You will also practice asking and answering "How are you?" and using I am / you are in English.
intro_mn: Та гэж ахмад хүнтэй хүндэтгэлтэй, чи гэж найзтайгаа чөлөөтэй мэндлэхийг сурна. Мөн англи хэлээр "How are you?" гэж асууж, хариулах, "I am / you are" хэлбэрийг хэрэглэхийг дадна.

grammar.title_en: Та vs чи: polite and informal "you"; English "to be"
grammar.title_mn: Та ба чи: хүндэтгэлтэй ба энгийн "you"; англи хэлний "to be"
grammar.explain_en: Mongolian has two words for "you". Use та with elders, teachers, strangers and in formal situations. Use чи with close friends, classmates and children. When unsure, choose та. Та can also be plural "you all". The answer is usually "Сайн байна" (I am fine); with та you ask "Сайн байна уу?", with a friend you can say just "Сайн уу?".
grammar.explain_mn: Англи хэлэнд "you" гэдэг ганц үг байдаг тул та, чи гэсэн ялгаа байхгүй. Харин "to be" үйл үг хүнээс хамаарч өөрчлөгдөнө: I am, you are, he/she is. Монголоор "Би сайн" гэж хэлдэг ч англиар заавал "I am fine" гэнэ. Асуухдаа "How are you?" гэж хэлээд, "I'm fine, thank you" гэж хариулна.

fill_blank.explain_en: A teacher is respected, so use polite та.
Between friends, informal чи is natural.
You are talking about yourself, so use би (I).
fill_blank.explain_mn: Өөрийнхөө тухай ярьж байгаа тул "би" хэрэглэнэ.

fill_blank.explain_en: You takes are, whether polite or informal.
fill_blank.explain_mn: "You" нь хүндэтгэлтэй ч, энгийн ч байсан "are" авна.

culture_note.en: In Ulaanbaatar, people use та with elders, teachers, colleagues and strangers, and чи with close friends and people their own age. Calling an older man ах or an older woman эгч shows warmth and respect. Switching to чи too early with an older person can sound rude.
culture_note.mn: Улаанбаатарт ахмад хүн, багш, хамт олон, танихгүй хүнтэй та гэж, дотны найз, үеийнхэнтэйгээ чи гэж ярьдаг. Ах, эгч гэж дуудах нь дотно бөгөөд хүндэтгэлтэй сонсогдоно. Ахмад хүнд эрт "чи" гэж хэлбэл бүдүүлэг сонсогдож болно.

review.notes: Mostly fine content, but a mismatched Mongolian grammar title, an unnatural 'Та сайн уу', a few unfaithful alt translations, and a Saruul/Saraa name inconsistency needed fixing.

opus_fix.notes: Main fixes: inconsistent та/чи register in the dialogue, a duplicate alternative sentence, and a title and culture note that didn't match between languages.

changes.why: The alternative was identical to the main sentence.
title_mn also covers "to be", so the English title has to match it.
Register: Bat is older and later says чиний to Saruul, so he should use чи here, not та.
Bat already greeted Saruul, so a second greeting is unnatural.
Updated to match the corrected Mongolian line.
Aligned with mn: the Mongolian version says 'peers', not 'family of the same age'.
